cards.explanation: The answer is the train of His robe. Isaiah says the Lord is seated on a throne, high and exalted, and the train of His robe fills the temple (Isaiah 6:1). The whole temple, friends. I can barely get my apron on without knocking over a cooling rack. Isaiah tells it as plainly as he saw it.

The answer is False. Each seraph has six wings, and Isaiah says that with two they cover their faces, with two they cover their feet, and with two they are flying (Isaiah 6:2). So only two of the six are doing the flying, friends. The other four are busy covering.

The answer is that He is holy. The seraphim call out, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.” (Isaiah 6:3) They're calling to one another, and holy is the word they keep saying. I think when creatures with six wings repeat a word, it's worth remembering.

The answer is False. They don't stay still. Isaiah says that at the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook (Isaiah 6:4). That's doorposts and thresholds shaking from voices alone, friends. I've never had a doorpost shake at anything I've said, and I've said some LOUD things.

The answer is smoke. Isaiah says the temple was filled with smoke at the sound of their voices, while the doorposts and thresholds were shaking (Isaiah 6:4). He doesn't say where the smoke came from, so I won't either. I'll just say it sounds like a day I would not want to be in a bakery.

The answer is that he is a man of unclean lips. Isaiah says, “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips…” (Isaiah 6:5). He says it because his eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts. I think seeing the King made him look at himself honestly.

The answer is False. Isaiah says he is “…a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips…” (Isaiah 6:5). He doesn't say he's the only one, and he doesn't say his people are fine. I like that he doesn't point fingers and just says what's true.

The answer is mouth. Isaiah says the seraph touched his mouth with the coal and said, “Now that this has touched your lips…” (Isaiah 6:7). That's the same place Isaiah named when he said he was a man of unclean lips.

The answer is that his iniquity is removed. The seraph says, “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.” (Isaiah 6:7) Isaiah had just called himself ruined. The seraph tells him his iniquity is gone.

The answer is that he offers to go himself. The Lord asks, “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” and Isaiah says, “Here am I. Send me!” (Isaiah 6:8). Isaiah volunteers himself, friends. I'd have needed at least three minutes and a cookie.

The answer is understand. The message is, “Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.” (Isaiah 6:9) They keep hearing and keep seeing, but they never understand. It's a heavy line, and I'll leave it as heavy as the Lord says it.

The answer is that they might turn and be healed. The Lord says, “Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.” (Isaiah 6:10) Turning and being healed is the outcome the Lord names there. I think this is a heavy part, so read it slowly.

The answer is False. There's no word about a next king. The Lord answers, “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged…” (Isaiah 6:11). It's a long answer to a short question. I think this one hurts to read.

The answer is unoccupied. The Lord says, “…until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged…” (Isaiah 6:11). The cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, and the houses are left empty too. It's a quiet, heavy picture.

The answer is False. The Lord says, “And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again.” (Isaiah 6:13) A tenth remains, but it isn't spared from the burning. The stump picture later in that same verse is where something is still left.

The answer is a stump. The Lord says, “As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.” (Isaiah 6:13) A stump is what's left when the tree comes down. The holy seed is that stump, still in the land.
